The character, reduced to what survives 16 pixels

One vector master becomes the favicon, the web app icon, the Android launcher icon and the Play listing. Same drawing every time, generated rather than exported by hand, so nothing drifts.

brand/mark/bilby-mark.svg25 outputsone generator

01 · The reduction

Four elements kept, everything else dropped

At launcher size the silhouette is the only thing most people ever consciously receive. Every element past the fourth costs it.

Two ears

Drawn as ellipses, not tapered points. A pointed ear reads as a fox and loses the animal entirely.

The helmet

The one shape that survives every crop a launcher can apply.

The antenna

Bulb deliberately oversized against the render. A true to scale bulb disappears below 48 pixels.

The visor

Wider than tall, sitting low, which is what makes the helmet read as a face rather than an egg.

Body and limbs

Unreadable below 96 pixels and they fight the square.

Signal arcs and planet

They belong to the hero image, where there is room for them.

02 · The honest test

Shown at real pixels, not scaled up

Every image below is at its actual size. This is the only test that matters, and it is the one most icon presentations quietly skip.

03 · Android

Every crop a launcher might apply

The adaptive canvas is 108dp and only the central 72dp is guaranteed. The mark fills 62 percent, so no launcher takes an ear tip off.

circle
squircle
rounded square

Themed icon, one ink

Android 13 and later recolours the launcher icon to the wallpaper. A flat silhouette of this mark would be an anonymous blob with ears, so the visor is subtracted from the shape and the eyes and smile are added back. The face survives in a single colour.

The header lockup uses the single ink version, not the full colour icon. A cream helmet on a cream page has no edge; the ink mark keeps the face because the visor is a hole rather than a dark shape, so the page shows through it.
